title: oku page
description: Source of truth for one renderable page. Authored as JSON; the kit's renderer maps the tree to Custom-Element DOM at load time.

$schema.description: Optional schema URL for editor autocomplete.

schema_version.description: Reader uses this to detect forward-compat issues.

title.description: Becomes the document <title> and the page cover's <h1>.

accent.description: Per-page accent token. Either a kit-known name (teal, amber, indigo, ...) or a CSS color value.

blocks.description: Top-level content sequence: cover-level elements (tldr) then sections.

eyebrow.description: Small label above the title, e.g. 'Implementation plan'.

updated.description: Last-updated date — quiet trust signal under the cover meta row.

lang.description: Per-page language override; otherwise project default applies.

summary.description: One-line summary, surfaced in nav tooltips and llms.txt.

id.description: Anchor + TOC key. Should be unique within the page.

lead.description: Optional one-paragraph lead under the heading.

example.description: Code + rendered-result pair. Renders as a two-column grid (code on the left, live output on the right) on wide screens; collapses to a stacked layout below ~900px. Use to document every primitive in reference.json so the JSON shape and the visible result sit side-by-side.

title.description: Optional small label shown above the pair.

output.description: The block that the code on the left produces when run. Schema accepts any contentBlock, so a code example can demonstrate a callout, a chart, a table, etc.

bind.description: Shared key for the cross-block hover-sync feature. Any two blocks with the same bind key flash together when either is hovered or focused.

view.description: Pin the initial view shown by the table-chrome view toggle. Defaults to 'table'. Use 'board' on tables whose primary point is the kanban grouping — otherwise the reader sees a flat table by default and the kanban shape stays one click away.

rows.description: Flat row form. Use either rows OR groups, not both.

groups.description: Grouped row form — chrome.js renders each group title as a subhead row across the views.

tableHeader.description: Either a plain header label (string / inline-array) or an object form with optional chip-filter and/or board-lane-order declarations.

values.description: Ordered chip values for chip-filter columns. Cells should declare one (or more) of these via the object cell form.

boardOrder.description: When this column drives the board view's group-by, render lanes in this order. Values present in row data but missing from boardOrder render at the end in first-occurrence order.

wrap.description:
When true, cells in this column honour explicit newlines (\n) in source content via `white-space: pre-line`. Use for narrative columns where the author wants multi-line cell content without inlining
tags.

tableRow.description: Row payload — either a positional array of cells or an object with cells + optional row-level affordances (link target, classes).

tableCell.description: Either a plain rich-string value or an object form carrying explicit chip values (supports multi-valued cells).

values.description: Chip values for this cell. May contain multiple to mark the row against more than one chip.

source.description: Code body. Use (1), (2)... as inline markers; each matches an annotation by id. Annotations may also declare `lines` / `match` externally and skip the inline marker.

lines.description: Optional line spec — '3' for a single line, '1-3' for a range, '1,5-7' for mixed. Hovering the marker highlights every listed line; when no inline (N) marker is present, the chip auto-places on the first listed line. Line numbers are 1-based and match the gutter.

match.description: Optional substring(s) of the source. Each occurrence is highlighted on marker hover, so you can point at a token without polluting the source with (N).

href.description: Optional. When set, the entire step card is wrapped in an anchor pointing here — keyboard reachable, click-targetable, no 'Open X' link text needed in content.

compare-grid.description: N-card comparison grid. Pick the card accent via verdict (or accent — alias). Mix content (rich text body), items (bullet list), and blocks (any contentBlock — callouts, code, charts, tables) freely; they render in source order. Both verdict and accent are optional and default to neutral.

verdict.description: Quality / scope shorthand: good (success border), bad (danger), in (success — was scope-grid status:in), out (muted), neutral (default). Use `accent` instead when you need to match the broader kit token vocabulary; both fields are honoured but accent wins on conflict.

accent.description: Card accent in the kit's standard color tokens. Wins over verdict if both are set. Use this when verdict's good/bad/in/out feels too arbitrary — accent maps directly to the same colour vocabulary as charts and callouts.

href.description: Optional anchor (e.g. `#chart-line`) — when set, the whole card becomes a clickable link to that target. Used by the charts page Pick-by-family grid so each variant mini-card jumps to its full example.

content.description: Rich-text body. Combine with items / blocks, or use any subset alone.

items.description: Bullet list inside the card. Renders below content when both are present.

blocks.description: Rich block content inside the card — callouts, code samples, tables, charts, anything from contentBlock. Renders after items. Use blocks when a card needs a worked example or a structured comparison; use items for a plain bullet list.

chart.description: Data-driven chart. The `type` field picks the render mode: Cartesian (scatter / line / area / bubble / quadrant) share an SVG plot with axes, pan, zoom, log scale, and PNG export; bar variants render label/value bars; donut renders a distribution arc. Each type has its own payload shape — the renderer dispatches by `type` so unused fields are simply ignored.

type.description: Render mode. Canonical types: plot (Cartesian, marks-composed) and arc (radial slice, mode-switched). Sugar aliases — scatter/line/area desugar to plot+marks; pie/donut desugar to arc+mode; stacked-bar/grouped-bar desugar to bar+mode. Aliases keep working AND let the author override any preset (e.g. type=pie + arc.end=270 for a 3/4 pie). Other types (bubble / quadrant / bar / heatmap / sparkline / waffle / gauge / radar / box-plot / bullet / slope / histogram / calendar-heatmap / treemap / ridgeline / funnel / sankey / network / scatter-matrix / parallel-coordinates / chord / geo) keep their existing payload shapes.

marks.description: For Cartesian (canonical type=plot, or alias scatter/line/area): which marks to draw. dots = scatter points, line = connecting line, area = fill under the line. Combine freely (e.g. ["dots", "line"] = line with point markers). Defaults: scatter→[dots], line→[line], area→[line, area], plot→[dots].

data.description: Canonical record-array input — alternative to the legacy `series: [{data: [{x, y}]}]` shape. Each record is a flat object; the `encoding` field maps column names to visual channels. Mark-composition uses the same `marks` list. Currently supported for the plot family (canonical type=plot or alias scatter/line/area). Desugars internally to series-grouped-by-encoding.color.

encoding.description: Field-to-channel mapping for canonical record-array input. Names of fields in each `data` record drive the visual channels.

x.description: Field name for the x-axis position.

y.description: Field name for the y-axis position.

color.description: Field name that groups records into colour series (one rendered series per distinct value).

size.description: Field name for the bubble-size channel (when relevant).

label.description: Field name carrying a per-record label (shown in tooltips).

mode.description: Sub-mode for canonical types. bar: single | stacked | grouped. arc: pie | donut. Defaults inferred from legacy alias when applicable (stacked-bar→stacked, donut→donut).

arc.description: Arc-family geometry overrides for type=arc / pie / donut. Defaults to a full 360° starting at 12 o'clock. Set start/end in degrees (clockwise from 12) for a partial arc.

inner_radius.description: For type=arc / pie / donut: inner-ring radius as fraction of outer radius. 0 = pie, ~0.55 = donut. Override the mode default — e.g. type=pie + inner_radius=0.3 renders a thick ring.

orientation.description: For charts whose layout has both forms (bar / column = horizontal vs vertical bars; histogram / column-histogram; box-plot rotation; violin rotation): switch the layout axis. Bar charts default to horizontal (rows). Set 'vertical' for column charts. Charts that don't support both axes ignore this property.

x_label.description: Cartesian only (scatter / line / area / bubble / quadrant).

series.description: Cartesian or stacked-bar / grouped-bar series. For Cartesian: each series carries `data: [{x, y, label, size?}]`. For stacked-bar / grouped-bar: each series carries `values: [number]` aligned to `categories`.

size.description: Bubble only. Drives the dot radius (sqrt-scaled so dot area is proportional to size).

values.description: stacked-bar / grouped-bar payload — one numeric value per entry in `categories`.

rows.description: Shared key carrying per-row payloads for bar (single bar per row), dot-plot, lollipop, dumbbell. Each row's required fields vary by chart type: bar / dot-plot / lollipop need {label, value}; dumbbell needs {label, from, to}. Color is a kit token where supported.

display.description: Override the right-hand readout (e.g. '95 / 100' instead of '95').

max.description: Bar / stacked-bar / grouped-bar — full-width value. Gauge — arc end (required). Defaults to the largest row value (bar) or the largest category total (stacked) / category max (grouped).

categories.description: stacked-bar / grouped-bar — ordered list of category labels (rows of the chart). Each series.values[] index aligns to this list.

quadrants.description: Quadrant chart only. Splits the plot into four regions with reference lines at (x, y) and optionally names each quadrant.

x.description: Vertical reference line position on the x-axis.

y.description: Horizontal reference line position on the y-axis.

labels.description: Four labels in order [top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right]. Use empty strings to skip a corner.

slices.description: donut / pie only. Each slice is a labelled value; the renderer normalises to 100%.

cells.description: heatmap only. 2D matrix — outer array is rows, inner array is columns. Length of outer ≥ 1; every inner row must have the same length.

row_labels.description: heatmap row labels (left edge). Length should match cells.length when supplied.

col_labels.description: heatmap column labels (top edge). Length should match cells[0].length when supplied.

scale.description: heatmap palette family. sequential is one-sided (low → high), diverging is two-sided (negative ← centre → positive).

domain.description: heatmap value domain [min, max] for the colour mapping. Defaults to the data's own min / max.

values.description: sparkline only. Sequence of numeric values rendered as an inline line / area / bar.

variant.description: sparkline render variant. Defaults to line.

end_label.description: sparkline only. Small caption shown to the right of the curve (e.g. ‘62%’, ‘↗’).

total.description: waffle / bullet — denominator. waffle: cell count when segments don't sum to it. bullet: max value.

segments.description: waffle / funnel segments. Each carries a label + count; cells coloured by category.

value.description: gauge — current value. Mapped onto a semicircular arc between min and max.

label.description: gauge / bullet — caption rendered under the value.

zones.description: gauge / bullet — coloured threshold bands rendered behind the value track.

label.description: Optional short label rendered above the band (gauge) or in the band's hover title — names the zone so the reader doesn't have to guess what 'the green slice' means.

axes.description: radar — N spokes radiating from centre. Each carries a label and optional per-axis max.

boxes.description: box-plot — one box per row. Carries quartiles + whiskers + optional outliers.

tracks.description: bullet — one row per metric. Each: { label, value, target?, max, zones? }.

items.description: slope — one entity per row, two paired values.

bins.description: histogram — pre-binned numeric distribution. Each entry: {lo, hi, count}. Bins should be contiguous and sorted by lo.

year.description: calendar-heatmap — calendar year to render. If absent, derived from the keys of `date_values` (assumes all share the same year).

date_values.description: calendar-heatmap — map of ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) → numeric value. Days absent from the map render as empty cells.

tree.description: treemap — flat list of leaves; one rectangle per entry, area proportional to `value`. Nested recursion via optional `children` is reserved for a later schema version.

distributions.description: ridgeline — one row per distribution; each is a small histogram-like ridge. `values` is a flat sample (each cell counted with a fixed bin width derived from the global min/max).

stages.description: funnel — ordered conversion stages. Each: {label, value, color?}. Drop-off between adjacent stages is shown as a tapered band.

nodes.description: sankey / network — node list. Each: {id (string, unique), label?, color?}. For sankey, the renderer derives left-to-right column placement from the link graph (BFS depth). For network, position is force-relaxed at render time from the link adjacency.

links.description: sankey / network — directed link list. Each: {source, target, value?, label?}. source and target reference node ids. value drives the ribbon thickness (sankey) or edge weight (network).

variables.description: scatter-matrix / parallel-coordinates — variable definitions. Each: {key, label?, domain?: [lo, hi]}. domain is optional — when omitted the renderer derives it from records.

records.description: scatter-matrix / parallel-coordinates — record list. Each record is an object keyed by variable id. Optional `_label` and `_color` (one of accent / warn / danger / success / muted) tag the record visually.

groups.description: chord — node list (each row + column in the flow matrix). Each: {id, label?, color?}. Order in this array defines the perimeter sequence going clockwise from 12 o'clock.

matrix.description: chord — N×N flow matrix. Row i carries the outgoing flows from groups[i]; matrix[i][j] is the flow from groups[i] to groups[j]. Cells default to 0 when omitted.

regions.description: geo — region values. Each: {id (region code), value, label?}. The renderer looks each id up in its built-in tile cartogram (Alpha-2 country codes plus the synthetic 'OTH' bucket for uncovered regions).

id.description: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 country code (US, GB, DE, BR, ...) or one of the kit's synthetic region tokens.

rows_dot.description: dot-plot — { rows: [{ label, value, color? }] }. Compact one-axis comparison; one row per dot.

values_dist.description: density / beeswarm / violin support — { values: [...] } at the chart root for density + beeswarm, or { distributions: [{ label, values, color? }] } for violin (and ridgeline).

ohlc.description: candlestick — { entries: [{ date, open, high, low, close }] }.

tree_sunburst.description: sunburst — { tree: nested { label, value, children } } (or root). Same shape as treemap.

marimekko_payload.description: marimekko — { categories, series: [{ label, values }] }. Same shape as stacked-bar; column widths scale with column totals.

stream_payload.description: stream — { categories, series: [{ label, values }] }. Same shape as stacked-bar; layers centre around the x-axis.

values.description: Shared key carrying raw numeric values for distribution / sparkline charts: density / beeswarm / sparkline / histogram (binning needed).

distributions.description: Shared key carrying per-distribution payloads for ridgeline / violin: [{ label, values, color? }].

entries.description: candlestick — list of { date, open, high, low, close }.

tree.description: treemap / sunburst — nested tree of { label, value, children? }.

bandwidth.description: density / violin — KDE bandwidth override (defaults to Silverman's rule).

sample_count.description: density — number of x-positions to sample (default 100).

tasks.description: gantt — [{label, start, end, color?}]. start/end are numeric (interpret per data).

tick_format.description: gantt — 'date' formats numeric ticks as ISO YYYY-MM-DD (treating numbers as Unix ms).

source.description: Mermaid source. Sequence / flow / state / gantt / class supported.

richString.description: Either a plain string or an array mixing strings with inline nodes.

lang.description: Override the project language for this instance.

oneOf.description: Sanitised inline HTML pass-through. The Markdown converter emits this for tags inside the small allowlist (a, code, em, strong, span, sup, sub, br, mark, kbd, samp, del, ins, abbr); the renderer drops the text into an inline span via innerHTML. Authors writing JSON pages should prefer the typed inline kinds — html is the markdown escape hatch, not a recommended primitive.
